the rate of uric-acid production by rat hepatocytes is a highly sensitive index of cell ATP homeostatic status, that this is irrespective of whether cell inorganic phosphate is lowered or raised, and that this suggests that raised plasma levels of uric-ac-id may be a marker, and perhaps also a cause, of compromised hepatic energy homeostasis.
uric acid production by rat hepatocytes is a marker of compromised cell ATP and Pi homeostasis, and is associated with NAFLD.
the rate of uric production from endogenous purine substrates is a sensitive marker of compromised cell ATP and Pi homeostasis and is increased in pathophysiological conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, sensitive, and noninvasive marker of hepatic ATP homeostatasis.
the regulation of uric acid synthesis and degradation by hepatocytes.
the role of uric acid in metabolic syndrome and NAFLD and with its potential as a diagnostic marker of compromised hepato-ATP homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
uric acid production in hepatocytes is a good marker of the metabolic status of ATP and Pi in hepatocytes.

uric acid is a sensitive index for the assessment of hepatic ATP homeo-stasis and that it may be an important factor in the pathogenesis of NAFLD and other pathologies associated with insulin resistance.
the production of purines, inosine, and uric acid by the liver is an important marker for compromised ATP homeostasis in the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
uric acid production is a very sensitive indicator of hepatocellular ATP depletion and that it may be a useful marker for compromised liver function.
plasma uric acid is a marker of compromised liver cell energy metabolism and that the rate of uricacid production by hepatocytes in vitro is an index of the severity of compromised ATP homeostasis.

the rate of uric-acid production by hepatocytes in vitro is a sensitive index for compromised ATP homeostasis in hepatocytes, irrespective of whether the ATP level is decreased or the inorganic phosphate level is raised.
The main takeaway from our work is that
plasma uric acid levels are a sensitive marker of compromised hepateocellular ATP homeostasis and are a potential marker of NAFLD.

the rate of production of the end-product of purine degradation (i.e., uric acid) by hepatocytes is highly sensitive to changes in the homeostasis of ATP and/or Pi and that it is a potentially useful marker of compromised ATP homeostasis in the liver.
uric acid production by hepatocyte is a very sensitive indicator of the status of hepatocellular ATP homeostasis, irrespective of the direction of change in cell Pi.
